speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pregnant patient presenting with vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me how many weeks pregnant you are and how long the bleeding has been going on?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Placenta Accreta.

Given your history of a prior cesarean section and the sudden onset of severe painless (or painful) bleeding with ceased contractions at 38 weeks, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of placenta accreta. I need to see the ultrasound images immediately to confirm the location of the placenta and any abnormal invasion into the uterine wall.
